notes: Web3 phase 2, W2: order quotes and an approval gate. The product can now place an order - and only an order - through a prepare/approve/execute split enforced in code, not configuration. exchange_prepare_order is a dry run: validation, a live order-book walk (VWAP, slippage in basis points, an honest depth verdict), the venue's own fee quote when its key is configured (an unavailable quote is reported as unknown, never guessed and never folded into a threshold), notional, and the auto-approval verdict; it then stores a plan. exchange_execute_order takes a plan id and NOTHING else - every parameter is read back from the stored plan, so no prompt, settings value or environment variable can rewrite an order between approval and execution. It fails closed in order (plan exists -> not expired, TTL 900s -> status approved -> auto approvals re-check the day's ledger) and only then sends, while holding the store lock, so one plan can never be sent twice; a failed send leaves the plan retryable and never touches the ledger. Default thresholds are web3.auto_usd_per_tx = 0 and web3.auto_usd_daily = 0 = every plan waits for a human, and MARKET orders never auto-approve at any threshold. Approval exists only in the console behind the Bearer WEB_TOKEN write gate (POST /api/exchange/plans/<id>); the model has no approve path - exchange_plans exposes list and cancel only. Withdrawals and on-chain transfers do not exist anywhere in the product: no function, no endpoint, no settings key, asserted by the core suite against the source file. The plan store is one atomic JSON file with a Beijing-date daily ledger, a 15-minute TTL and a 50-plan cap. Third venue: Binance. Binance has no official MCP or agent API (the official GitHub organisation search returned zero MCP repositories on 2026-10-24) - only the official Skills Hub and REST - so this is our own thin adapter over the documented REST surface: public depth, signed account and openOrders reads, and hex HMAC-SHA256 over the query string for order placement with X-MBX-APIKEY in the header. The catalog now carries nine venues and the capability block reports honestly: read_only false, orderable okx/kraken/binance, order_gate prepare -> console approval -> execute, withdrawals false, onchain_transfers false. The console Exchange view gains a pending-plan panel - a threshold row (per-transaction cap, daily cap, today's spent USD), plan cards with venue, side, symbol, type, quantity, price, notional, slippage, fee, status, reason and expiry, approve/reject on a pending plan and cancel on an approved one - plus an honest empty state, and the disclosure copy now states the W2 truth while keeping the four-part disclosure (the product is permanently free but exchange fees and gas are not zero / not investment advice / risk borne by the user / credentials stay on this machine). Settings gain the web3 caps block (both keys required, numbers 0..1000000, fail-closed zeros). A new binance-read-only skill pack and a rewritten docs/features/exchanges.md document the protocol contracts, the approval semantics and the honest boundaries.
